binding.what: The agent samples the slot's single mutable shard every 0.5 s instead of shipping every saved wave (suspected cause of M2-P2-NO-COMMON-WAVE: two slots can ship disjoint steps before a kill)
binding.ruling: Replaced (human decision 2026-10-09, no experiment gate: the recorded exploratory data in .factory/runs/M2/wave-exp-tree.json showed both 'unseen' and 'race', and the redesign removes both) by event-driven shipping of every committed wave in ascending step order, woken by the stage's WT_WAVE line and by a backstop scan each supervise pass; no shipper reads the legacy pair again. Proven by the causal closure (GATES causal-pre-fix-has-symptom on the tree immediately before wave-ship-restore, causal-fixed-tree-clean on the fixed tree).

binding.what: The shipper copies the mutable legacy shard and brackets the copy with two sidecar reads (seqlock); a copy that races a newer save is skipped (the alternative hypothesis)
binding.ruling: Ships only committed, immutable wave directories as a unit: one CKPT_PART per file listed in wave.json (each with its sha256) and then one CKPT carrying the wave.json manifest; nothing that can be rewritten is read, so no copy can race a save. The before/after sidecar bracket goes with the path that needed it.

binding.what: save_shard seqlock writes the one mutable shard per slot (the legacy pair) that resume, the oracle readers and the shipper all read today
binding.ruling:
Demoted to a derived alias for the oracle readers only (BA-13): link_legacy(wave_dir) hard-links (copy fallback) the wave's state.pt onto _ckpt_rankp

.pt through save_shard's seqlock order and writes the .step.json from wave.json's step. Resume and shipping never read it; wave.json is the only step binding.

binding.what: The stage writes each checkpoint over the same path, prints nothing the agent can wake on, and checkpoints the last step twice when steps % ckpt_every == 0 (periodic save at stage.py:1082-1083, unconditional final save at :1089)
binding.ruling:
Every save commits an immutable wave out_dir/waves//rp

/step-/ (state.pt first, wave.json with per-file sha256 last, directory renamed into place), then links the alias, then prints WT_WAVE . commit_wave on a step the slot has already committed writes nothing and returns committed=False; the stage prints WT_WAVE only for a new commit, so the final save of an already-committed last step is a no-op and no committed directory is ever removed or replaced. The slot keeps its newest 3 committed waves.

binding.what: Resume reads the legacy pair and refuses a shard its sidecar does not name
binding.ruling: Two legs, each consistent on its own. wave-stage-write keeps _resume on the alias, which link_legacy derives byte for byte from the newest committed wave and every RESTORE rewrites (so heal and restart-in-place resume exactly as today while the agent still restores the legacy pair). wave-resume, which depends on wave-ship-restore (the task that makes RESTORE wave-based and sets resume_step), rebuilds resume on the wave (RUNTIME-I12's 'the manifest is the wave's sidecar'): it reads the committed wave of spec.resume_step (the newest committed wave when resume_step is None, local mode) through validate_wave and refuses, before any state is applied, a missing wave directory, a missing or unparsable wave.json, a wave.json naming another step, a listed file missing or with another sha256 or size, or a file present but not listed; it never reads the alias. The two phase-2 refusal tests are ported to the wave input in wave-resume with the same assertions (HANDOUT §8 'Ported tests').

binding.what: Committed waves of an abandoned timeline stay on disk: after a resume from step n, the slot's waves newer than n; after a launch from step 0 (resume false, e.g. a heal with no common wave), every wave the slot committed before. Because commit_wave writes nothing for a step already committed, the new timeline would silently keep the old timeline's wave under that step
binding.ruling: A resume from step n removes the slot's committed waves newer than n before its first step; a launch with resume false removes every committed wave of the slot under its tag before its first step; both log the dropped steps (wave-stage-write, kept by wave-resume).

binding.what: RESTORE replaces the shard and sidecar while the slot's stage may be alive, outside the ship lock, leaks the body on a malformed step, and does not mark the restored wave as shipped (M2-P2-RESTORE-LIVE-STAGE, -RESTORE-BODY-LEAK, -SHIP-SPANS-RESTORE, -RESTORE-RESHIP)
binding.ruling: Two deliveries. Verdict-independent, on the legacy pair (restore-hardening, before the gated chain): _on_restore refuses (RESTORE_ACK ok=false, reason names the live stage) while the slot's stage is alive, runs under _ship_lock, refuses a missing or non-integer step, unlinks the received body on every exit path (try/finally), and records the restored (run_id, rank, peer, step) in _shipped. On waves (wave-ship-restore): RESTORE becomes a wave transfer (RESTORE_PART per listed file, then RESTORE with the manifest) that keeps every one of those properties, verifies every file's sha256 and the manifest step, commits with commit_received_wave and links the alias; a local committed wave of the same step whose manifest differs is refused loudly, an equal one is kept untouched.

binding.what: _shipped, the per-agent record of shipped waves, and the ship lock shared by the supervisor and ABORT
binding.ruling: Per (run_id, rank, peer, step); shared by supervisor, WT_WAVE wake-up, ABORT and RESTORE under one lock; ABORT ships every committed, unshipped wave in order before acknowledging.

binding.what: The coordinator's checkpoint store: one file per slot per step, common_step and prune
binding.ruling:
Rebuilt to hold waves: (slot, step) -> root/rp

/step-/ with wave.json and its files, committed by rename only after every listed file's sha256 and the manifest's step verify; index/common_step/prune read committed waves only; a wave with any mismatch is refused (CONTROL-I8 corrupt-shard rule, per file). A unit test pins that common_step over waves shipped in order is the newest step every slot shipped.

binding.what: CKPT intake takes rank and peer from the message and never checks the attempt (M2-P1-CKPT-IDENTITY)
binding.ruling: Slot and attempt come from the connection (_slot_for); a CKPT (and later every CKPT_PART) whose rank/peer disagree with the connection's slot, or of another attempt, is dropped, logged and its body unlinked.

binding.what: RESULT intake takes rank and peer from the message
binding.ruling: Slot from the connection; a RESULT naming another slot is dropped and logged.

binding.what: A request's reply is accepted from any connection that knows its rid
binding.ruling: _pending maps rid to (queue, node_id); a reply from any other worker's connection is dropped, logged and its body unlinked; the real reply is still accepted.

binding.what:
The oracle readers of final checkpoints: validation/state.py reads _ckpt_rankp

.pt; tests/helpers/exact.py globs out/*_ckpt_rank*p*.pt and reads its .step.json; test_coordinator.py:341-344 reads the replacement's restored pair
binding.ruling: Carried unchanged: the alias (BA-3) is written after every commit and every RESTORE, from the wave, so the readers see the same bytes and step as today; waves live under out/waves/ so no wave file matches the non-recursive glob. tests/helpers/exact.py is outside every task's scope and its sha256 9fcb6cb57fec968b9f348ae867a01567b20a095c1744ba4b43b9fb2464255e7d is checked by every task that runs a fleet.

binding.what: export_wave writes the coordinator's wave into engine layout for a local resume
binding.ruling: Rebuilt: writes the committed wave directory (wave.json and files, hashes verified) under out_dir/waves/... and then its alias, so a local resume reads the wave like any other.

binding.what: Local disk and control-link backlog when every wave is shipped (shipping slower than saving)
binding.ruling:
The stage keeps its newest 3 committed waves; a wave pruned before the agent shipped it is logged as '[agent ] ship gap rp

step=' and never skipped silently; the experiment and the GATES count gaps (0 expected).

binding.what: solve() raises a stage's measured activation budget to the 1F1B floor, so a tight budget over-commits memory instead of degrading
binding.ruling: Removed: the measured budget is used as is; a budget the heuristic cannot fit goes to the degrade path (BA-17).

binding.what: zero_bubble() raises when no grid candidate fits the budget; _manual_order raises on memory
binding.ruling: Degrade: search the largest per-stage warm-up (non-increasing down the pipeline) whose memory replay fits every budget, validated by simulate; return it with params.degraded, the warm-ups and the bubble; refuse only when one microbatch's F plus pending state exceeds a stage's budget, naming stage, need and budget in bytes.

binding.what: Per-attempt ownership and order the stage reads: mb_owner for routing, schedule_order for execution, peer_weights
binding.ruling: Rebuilt at the boundary: they may change only at a resume (between-step rebalancing), read from the attempt's spec; the fold order stays the microbatch index (runtime/accumulate.py), so the bytes do not move.

binding.what: ZeRO-1 optimizer-state ownership and its manifest mapping
binding.ruling: Carried unchanged across a rebalance: it depends on the peer index and width, never on mb_owner; a byte-exact resume-with-new-owner test proves it.

binding.what: RNG draws whose order could depend on ownership: torch global RNG saved per slot; data generator per (seed, step, mb)
binding.ruling: Carried unchanged: no training op draws the global RNG and the data RNG is keyed by (seed, step, mb), so ownership cannot reorder a draw; the resume test compares the RNG state by sha256.

binding.what: Nothing records under which recipe a shard was written; a resume under another partition or batch would load the wrong weights with every digest matching
binding.ruling: The state file records the recipe pins (model, seeds, data, microbatches, mb_size, seq_len, optimizer hyperparameters, precision, wire codec, recompute, steps, partition) plus 'zero1_widths' (stage_widths), which binds whole-tensor ZeRO-1 shards only because their names[k::w] depend on w; a logical-layout checkpoint (RUNTIME-I12, M2b) is width-free and checked through its manifest, and M2b drops this one pin for it. Resume refuses differing pins (or none) before applying any state, naming the field.

binding.what: patch_spec_for_resume pins everything except endpoints and devices
binding.ruling: Extended in three separately tested ways: resume_step names the wave every slot resumes from, set by heal and restart (wave-ship-restore) and by rebalance (rebalance-loop); slot_peers and trusted_peers are re-pinned to the attempt's nodes (slot-key-pinning); peer_weights, mb_owner and schedule_order are replaced only by an explicit ownership argument (rebalance-loop). Every other field stays pinned.

binding.what: Live per-step telemetry kept per run and per slot, consumed by nobody, and never reset between attempts, so after a heal or a rebalance it would still hold the dead node's or the old ownership's summaries
binding.ruling: Cleared under run.lock by every _launch (first launch, heal, restart, rebalance), so the window holds only the current attempt's summaries of its current owners; consumed by the rebalance decision only, read under run.lock, never trusted beyond CONTROL-I18's validation.

binding.what: Rebalancing shares the abort/restore/relaunch path and the attempt counter with heal and restart
binding.ruling: A rebalance is its own attempt kind, applied only on the _monitor thread (BA-45). After _abort_all it re-reads common_step, as _heal and _restart_in_place do (coordinator.py:1298, 1329), because ABORT ships every unshipped wave and the CKPT intake's prune then drops waves older than the new common step, the decided one included; it restores that re-read wave with resume_step, relaunches with the patched ownership (ownership does not depend on the step, so the decision stays valid), is recorded in run.replans, and never consumes max_restarts or max_heals; liveness starts the new attempt at wave+1 through the existing _launch path (CONTROL-I17 unchanged). If the re-read common_step is None the rebalance is abandoned and logged, never a restart from step 0.

binding.what: Mesh accept loop: any socket consumes one of n_in accept slots and its HELLO (st, pe) is trusted with no authentication, range or duplicate check (M2-P1-MESH-AUTH, focus fact a)
binding.ruling: Each accepted socket is authenticated in its own thread under a bounded handshake timeout; refused (closed, WT_P2P_REFUSED line and p2p_refused event) when the key fails, the authenticated id is not slot_peers[st][pe], st is outside {rank-1, rank}, pe is out of range or not higher than ours for intra, or (st, pe) is already bound; the loop keeps accepting until every expected (st, pe) is bound.

binding.what: Chain: one failed authentication raises and brings the stage down (focus fact b)
binding.ruling: The chain acceptor follows the mesh rule (BA-25): each accepted socket is authenticated in its own thread under the bounded handshake timeout and the listener keeps accepting until n = p2p_streams sockets whose authenticated id is slot_peers[rank-1][0] are bound; a socket that fails authentication, holds another id, or stays silent is refused, logged and closed without consuming a stream slot; when every expected socket is bound the listener and every still-pending socket are closed. Only the dial side, whose target is fixed, fails when the acceptor is not slot_peers[rank+1][0]. Stream identity needs no binding: fragments reassemble to the exact payload in any order across streams (TRANSPORT-I2).

binding.what: The mesh dialer sends its HELLO only after its own accepts complete, chaining boot delays into the acceptor's handshake timeout (focus fact g)
binding.ruling: The dial thread authenticates and sends the HELLO right after verification; wiring happens after all sockets are bound.

binding.what: trusted_peers exists in the spec but no code in src/ fills it; the key is per host, so a host's slots share one id (focus fact c)
binding.ruling: The coordinator pins slot_peers[stage][peer] (and trusted_peers) from the peer id each agent proved in its control handshake (BA-40); heal, restart and rebalance re-pin; a coordinator-run spec (endpoints set) without slot_peers is refused by the stage.

binding.what: The stage inherits the host-wide key path from the environment
binding.ruling: Per agent: the agent's key is <workdir>/peer_key (0600, atomic create), used for its control handshake (ctrl-mutual-auth) and passed to its stage explicitly as WANTRAIN_PEER_KEY (slot-key-pinning).

binding.what: peer_id depends on whether the optional blake3 module imports on that host (focus fact d)
binding.ruling: Fixed to SHA-256 (hashlib, always present): peer_id = sha256(pub)[:32 hex]; no optional dependency decides an identity.

binding.what: HMAC fallback returns 'hmac-anon' and silently ignores trusted_peers (focus fact e)
binding.ruling: Removed: cryptography is a hard dependency (pyproject.toml:15) and AEAD needs X25519; authenticate refuses when ed25519 is unavailable.

binding.what: Data-plane handshake: each side signs b'wantrain-auth|' + the peer's challenge, a symmetric message that a second connection can reflect
binding.ruling: Each side signs a role-tagged hash of the whole transcript (domain, both public keys, both challenges, both X25519 ephemerals) under a per-plane domain ('wantrain-p2p|v2|' or 'wantrain-ctl|v2|'); a peer challenge equal to ours is refused; per-direction session keys come from X25519 + HKDF-SHA256 over that transcript.

binding.what: token_mac: the worker's MAC uses one domain and one nonce; the same function would serve a coordinator proof (focus fact f)
binding.ruling: The worker's token MAC is HMAC(token, 'wantrain-control-worker|v3|' + transcript hash of the sealed control handshake); the coordinator never proves itself with the token: it proves its own ed25519 key (BA-42), so no token-derived value can be reflected between roles. Hex inputs are validated (exact length, lowercase).

binding.what: Coordinator handshake and agent connect use the shared MAC, the coordinator never proves itself, a worker accepts auth=false from anyone
binding.ruling: Rebuilt: TCP connect -> control-plane identity handshake (worker role, expect_peer = the pinned coordinator id; coordinator role, any worker key) -> both sides seal -> CHALLENGE{auth} -> HELLO{mac or session_mac} -> WELCOME, all inside the sealed channel. A worker holding a token refuses auth=false; a worker refuses a coordinator whose key is not the pinned id (required off loopback).

binding.what: The coordinator starts on 0.0.0.0 without a token and only warns
binding.ruling: Refused: start() raises without a token unless the coordinator binds a loopback address (local mode); the CLI reports it and exits non-zero.

binding.what: The control channel is plaintext and unauthenticated after the handshake: an on-path host could rewrite ASSIGN (and the pinned slot keys in it) or read waves
binding.ruling: Always sealed (loopback included) with the AEAD record layer under the keys of the control handshake, before the first message; send_file included.

binding.what: The reconnect HELLO carries the session secret in clear, and WELCOME sends it in clear
binding.ruling: WELCOME travels only inside the sealed channel; a reconnect sends session_mac = HMAC(session, 'wantrain-control-session|v3|' + transcript hash), never the session, compared in constant time, and is accepted only from the peer id the node registered with.

binding.what: Data-plane frames travel in plaintext over every chain, mesh and multi-stream socket
binding.ruling: Every socket is wrapped after authentication in a SecureSocket with its own per-direction keys and counters (multi-stream sockets each their own); END and half-close pass through; payload bytes delivered to the runtime are unchanged; the socket counts its seal and open time for the measured cost (BA-44).

binding.what: Local mode: run_local launches every slot on localhost with no coordinator, so no slot_peers
binding.ruling: Carried unchanged: endpoints None means local mode, authenticated and sealed, slot_peers optional (enforced when set).

binding.what: The slot's data-plane identity would travel as an unauthenticated HELLO field (peer_pub) that an on-path host could swap while keeping a MAC that covers only the nonces
binding.ruling: No identity field in HELLO: the coordinator takes the worker's peer id from the control handshake's verified ed25519 key (bound to the token MAC by the transcript) and stores it on the Worker; slot pinning reads only that.

binding.what: HELLO's endpoint and capability fields (advertise_host, data_port, listen/probe ports, declarations) decide where other slots dial
binding.ruling: Travel only inside the sealed, transcript-bound channel; a dial to a swapped address now fails the data-plane slot check (BA-25/26) instead of reaching an impostor.

binding.what: Coordinator identity: the coordinator has no key a worker could pin, so any holder of the token (every admitted worker) could pose as it
binding.ruling: The coordinator loads or creates <state_dir>/coord_key (0600) and prints 'COORDINATOR_ID <32 hex>' at start; workers take --coordinator-id (or WANTRAIN_COORD_ID) and pass it as expect_peer; a worker refuses to connect off loopback without it.

binding.what: CKPT_PART staging at the coordinator: parts of a wave wait for the CKPT that commits them
binding.where: new state introduced by BA-2/BA-9 (store root/.incoming/)
binding.ruling: Staged per connection slot and step; at most the files of 2 uncommitted steps per slot, each at most the size the manifest later declares; a part of another attempt, a duplicate name, a third open step, or a CKPT whose manifest lists a file not staged or with another sha256 drops the staged parts, logs and unlinks them (CONTROL-I18 style: the reader keeps reading).

binding.what: The AEAD cost on the step has no measurement point (focus item 5: cost < 1% of the step, measured)
binding.ruling: SecureSocket counts records, bytes and the nanoseconds spent sealing and opening; each slot prints one 'WT_AEAD' line at finish. validation/aead_cost.py measures the overlap-aware cost (sealed step wall time minus unsealed, interleaved pairs on the same seed, median with a distribution-free CI) per configuration and the serialized (seal+open)/steps_wall; on the toy both are MEASURED with no bound (the human's decision 2026-10-10, HANDOUT §2c); the unsealed arm exists only inside the validation tool's measurement process. Follow-up ADR: take the cipher off the critical path.

binding.what: Where a rebalance executes: the CKPT that completes a common wave is handled on that worker's own connection thread (_conn_loop -> _dispatch), whose replies (ABORT_ACK, RESTORE_ACK) only that same thread can deliver; heal and restart run on the _monitor thread
binding.ruling: The CKPT intake never decides or applies a rebalance. _monitor, the one thread that already owns heal and restart, evaluates the rule between judge passes when common_step has advanced past the last evaluated step and every slot has >= 4 accepted summaries, and applies it there; a convict or stall verdict in the same pass wins and the evaluation waits for the next attempt's window (cleared by _launch). Two attempt-changing actions can therefore never run at once.

binding.what:
The alias _ckpt_rankp

.pt becomes a hard link to a committed wave's state.pt; any writer that opened the alias for writing in place would write into the immutable wave
binding.where: src/wantrain/fault_tolerance/checkpoint.py:84-94 (save_shard: temp + os.replace), 182-195 (export_wave); src/wantrain/worker/agent.py:663-686 (_on_restore: os.replace onto the alias)
binding.ruling: Every alias writer replaces the directory entry (temp name + os.replace), never opens the alias for writing; link_legacy creates the link under a temp name and renames it over the alias; a test writes the alias through every writer and asserts the wave's sha256 is unchanged (wave-layout).

binding.what: Coordinator staging of CKPT_PART bodies before the CKPT that commits them is fed by admitted workers (CONTROL-I20 slot from the connection, BA-43 bounds); no earlier task tests them because CKPT_PART does not exist before wave-ship-restore
binding.where: new state introduced by BA-2/BA-9 (store root/.incoming/), coordinator.py _dispatch
binding.ruling: wave-ship-restore delivers both with tests that would fail on the message-trusting or unbounded mutant: a part sent on another slot's connection, a part of another attempt, a third open step, an oversized or duplicate part; each is dropped, logged and unlinked while the reader keeps reading.

tasks.title: Degrade instead of refusing under a tight activation budget (SCHEDULER-I13)

when no grid candidate fits, zero_bubble returns a schedule built from the largest per-stage warm-ups (non-increasing down the pipeline, at least 1) whose memory replay fits every max_mem, validated by simulate; params carry degraded=True, the warm-ups and the bubble

SCHEDULER-I1 golden orders and SCHEDULER-I2 bubble formulas still pass unmodified

tasks.objective: Let a resume change only peer weights, microbatch ownership and slot orders (plus addresses and slot keys) and continue byte-identically, while a state file written under different recipe pins is refused before any state is applied.

JobSpec.pins() returns the recipe pins (model config, init and data seeds, dataset, steps, microbatches, mb_size, seq_len, lr and optimizer hyperparameters, compute and boundary precision, wire codec, recompute, partition) plus 'zero1_widths' = stage_widths, documented in the code as binding whole-tensor ZeRO-1 shards only (names[k::w] depend on w; RUNTIME-I12 logical checkpoints are width-free and M2b drops this pin for them); _checkpoint stores pins in the payload; _resume compares them with its spec's before load_state_dict and refuses a mismatch naming the first differing field, and refuses a payload without pins

test_resume_refuses_changed_pins (microbatches, partition, zero1_widths) and test_resume_refuses_a_shard_without_pins: the refusal happens before any parameter, optimizer or RNG state changes; covers: RUNTIME-I15

tasks.title: Transcript-bound ed25519 + X25519 handshake per plane, SHA-256 ids, no HMAC fallback
tasks.objective: Make the handshake bind a plane domain, both identities, both challenges and both ephemeral keys under role-tagged signatures, derive per-direction session keys and the cipher, fix peer ids to SHA-256 and remove the HMAC fallback.
acceptance: peer_id(pub) = sha256(pub).hexdigest()[:32] on every host; blake3 is no longer imported; fingerprint_algo is 'sha256'

authenticate(sock, key_path=None, trusted_peers=None, expect_peer=None, aes_hw=False, domain='wantrain-p2p|v2|', role=None) exchanges pub, a 16-byte challenge (exact length, else refused) and an X25519 ephemeral; with role None the roles are the lower and higher challenge, with role 'worker' or 'coordinator' each side declares its role and complementary roles are required; a peer challenge equal to ours is refused; each side signs SHA-256 of domain + own role + both pubs + both challenges + both ephemerals in role order

it returns {peer_id, mode: 'ed25519', fingerprint_algo, cipher, send_key, recv_key, send_prefix, recv_prefix, transcript}: keys from HKDF-SHA256 over the X25519 secret with the transcript hash as salt and per-direction info; cipher is 'aes-256-gcm' iff both sides declared aes_hw else 'chacha20-poly1305'; the two ends' send/recv keys mirror

a peer id outside trusted_peers, or different from expect_peer, raises ConnectionError after the signature check; without ed25519 (cryptography missing) authenticate raises; there is no shared-token mode

tests: test_handshake_binds_transcript_and_derives_mirrored_keys, test_reflected_challenge_is_refused, test_signature_over_another_transcript_is_refused, test_p2p_and_control_domains_never_cross (a transcript signed under one domain fails under the other), test_roles_must_be_complementary, test_expect_peer_refuses_another_key, test_allowlist_refuses_an_unknown_peer (kept), test_peer_id_is_sha256_without_blake3, test_cipher_is_aes_only_when_both_ends_have_it, and test_hmac_fallback_has_no_default_token replaced by test_handshake_refuses_without_ed25519 (strictly stronger); covers: TRANSPORT-I5
verify: uv run pytest -q -p no:randomly tests/unit/test_codecs_identity.py -k "transcript or reflected or domains_never_cross or complementary or expect_peer or allowlist or sha256_without_blake3 or cipher_is_aes or refuses_without_ed25519"

tasks.title: AEAD record layer: AES-256-GCM with hardware AES, ChaCha20-Poly1305 fallback (TRANSPORT-I7)
tasks.objective: Provide a socket wrapper that seals every byte in AEAD records with counter nonces that never repeat, a deterministic rekey before the cipher's limit, measured seal/open time, and a per-core throughput benchmark.
acceptance: hardware_aes() is true only with AES-NI (x86 'aes' cpu flag) or ARMv8 AES (Linux aarch64 'aes' feature, macOS arm64 hw.optional.arm.FEAT_AES) and false when it cannot tell

SecureSocket(sock, cipher, send_key, recv_key, send_prefix, recv_prefix) offers sendall, recv, recv_into, shutdown, close, settimeout, setsockopt and fileno; it seals in records of at most 1 MiB plaintext framed as u32 length + ciphertext||tag; nonce = 4-byte prefix || 8-byte big-endian record counter per direction

tasks.title: Between-step rebalancing from telemetry at a common wave (SPEC-control task 2)
tasks.objective: Have the coordinator re-plan ownership and order from the current attempt's telemetry at a common wave when the predicted gain pays for the restart, apply it as its own attempt, and keep the run byte-identical.
acceptance: _launch clears run.telem_window under run.lock for every attempt (first launch, heal, restart, rebalance), so the window never holds a summary of an earlier attempt or owner; test_telemetry_window_starts_empty_each_attempt

the rule is evaluated only on the _monitor thread, between judge passes, when common_step has advanced past the last evaluated step and every slot has >= 4 accepted TELEM_STEP summaries in the window; the CKPT intake on a connection thread never decides or applies a rebalance (BA-45); a convict or stall verdict in the same pass is handled first and the evaluation waits for the next attempt

it applies the plan only when decision is true, (pred_cur_s - pred_new_s) * remaining_steps > 2 * restart_cost_s and len(run.replans) < cfg.max_replans (default 2); restart_cost_s is the measured duration of this run's last restore-to-first-step, else cfg.replan_restart_cost_s (default 30)

applying runs _abort_all, then re-reads common_step (ABORT ships newer waves and the intake's prune may drop the decided one, as _heal already handles), restores that wave and relaunches with patch_spec_for_resume(..., resume_step=step, ownership={peer_weights, mb_owner, schedule_order}); a None common step abandons the rebalance with a log line, never a restart from step 0; it is recorded in run.replans and RunResult.replans as {step, pred_cur_s, pred_new_s, owner_changed, peer_weights} and logged as 'REPLAN ...'; it consumes neither max_restarts nor max_heals
patch_spec_for_resume changes ownership only through that explicit argument; every other field stays pinned
